summary: ADD badge ships consistent with the pre-existing ticket-level ADD banner (claim verified, both bg-blue-600); suppression vs RE-FIRE correct; no hardcoded hex in diff; one polish concern: blue collides with dine_in order-type pill and yellow/amber is the kitchen 'attention' convention.

issues.problem: bg-blue-600 is a raw Tailwind utility, not a design token. The codebase exposes --color-warning (#FF9500 iOS orange) which is the conventional kitchen 'new/attention' signal (Toast/R Power use amber-family). Blue also visually collides with the dine_in ORDER_TYPE_COLORS pill at line 31 — on a dine-in ticket you get a blue 'Dine-In' header pill AND a blue 'ADD' inline badge, which dilutes the signal.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) re-skin both the new TicketItemRow ADD badge AND the existing ticket-level ADD banner (line 192) to bg-[var(--color-warning)] / amber-500 in a follow-up polish task, or (b) accept blue as an intentional Sear-brand signal but log a polish ticket to differentiate it from dine_in (e.g., outline ring instead of solid fill on one of them).

issues.problem: text-caption-2 is the smallest type token; on a wall-mounted KDS at arm's length the inline ADD pill may be hard to scan vs the header banner. Matches RE-FIRE pill sizing so internally consistent, but worth measuring on the actual KDS hardware.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider bumping inline badges to text-caption-1 in a future KDS legibility pass; not blocking.

benchmark_gap: Toast/R Power convention for 'new item added to existing ticket' is amber/yellow attention (matches the universal kitchen 'look here, this changed' semantic). Sear is using blue, which reads as informational/status rather than alert. Acceptable Sear-brand choice but documented gap.
